I don't have any notes on Isaiah 52 for you yet. My first try at fetching the commentary pages failed: my code crashed while reading the results, so I never saw any of the page text. Then the system stopped me from using the web tool for the rest of this turn.

I'm not supposed to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I can't write verse-by-verse notes from pages I haven't read. Anything I wrote now would be unsourced.

**Pages I tried to fetch (none read):**
- https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-52/
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/isaiah/52-1.htm
- https://www.preceptaustin.org/isaiah-52-commentary
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/isaiah/52.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/isaiah/52.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/isaiah/52.htm

**If you ask again, I'll go through the sources in this order:**
1. **The traditional reading:** Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** the main debates are likely to be:
   - v. 13–15: the Servant as Christ, the nation of Israel or both.
   - v. 15: whether "sprinkle" means cleansing or "startle."
   - v. 7: how Paul uses this verse in Romans 10.

   I'd look for each tradition's own teachers on Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Wesley's notes, Seedbed, Sam Storms, LCMS and 1517.
3. **Other views:**
   - Modern scholarship: the NET Bible notes (especially on "sprinkle" in v. 15) and Bible Odyssey on the Servant Songs.
   - Catholic and Orthodox: New Advent (Church Fathers), Catholic.com and OCA.
   - Debated popular teaching: only if the sites actually discuss it.

Every point would have its URL.
